speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born at 33 weeks of gestation. The newborn is presenting with respiratory distress 2 hours after birth. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy until premature onset of labor. There was no significant prenatal care history mentioned.

speaker: Doctor
text:
A 33-week preterm infant presenting with respiratory distress two hours after birth is highly suggestive of Hyaline Membrane Disease, also known as Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS), due to surfactant deficiency. To confirm this diagnosis and assess the severity, I need to see imaging and clinical signs of air leak or other complications.

The chest X-ray findings of fine reticular granulation and ground-glass appearance, combined with the preterm status and respiratory distress, are classic for Hyaline Membrane Disease. The arterial blood gas confirms respiratory acidosis and hypoxemia consistent with this condition.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Respiratory Distress Syndrome (Hyaline Membrane Disease)
